title: Entanglement, Evolutionary Stability, and Strategy-Space Dependence in an EWL Quantum Game
abstract: We examine how Eisert--Wilkens--Lewenstein (EWL) quantization affects evolutionary stability in a symmetric $2\times2$ game whose interior mixed Nash equilibrium is not evolutionarily stable. In the restricted two-parameter EWL strategy space, the quantum equilibrium $s^*=(π/2,π/4)$ becomes a strict symmetric Nash equilibrium, and hence an evolutionarily stable strategy, for every $γ>0$. Extending the admissible pure strategies to the full three-parameter $SU(2)$ family preserves the Nash equilibrium but introduces a continuum of payoff-neutral mutants, causing strictness and the second ESS condition to fail. Thus, entanglement stabilizes the equilibrium only within the restricted EWL strategy space; the effect does not survive enlargement to full $SU(2)$.
summary: This paper analyzes an EWL quantum game to determine how entanglement influences evolutionary stability. It finds that while entanglement stabilizes the equilibrium within a restricted strategy subspace, this stabilizing effect vanishes when the allowed strategies are expanded to the full SU(2) group. This demonstrates a strong dependence of dynamical stability on the assumed strategic domain.
main_problem: The study investigates how entanglement, introduced via EWL quantization, affects the evolutionary stability (ESS) of an interior mixed Nash equilibrium in a quantum game.
main_result: Entanglement successfully stabilizes the equilibrium as an ESS only within a restricted two-parameter strategy space; this stabilization fails when the strategy space is enlarged to the full SU(2) manifold.
method: The authors use concepts from evolutionary game theory (ESS criteria) applied to quantum games, comparing payoff gaps calculated under restricted versus full parameterizations of quantum strategies.
model_or_system: The model is a symmetric $2 	imes 2$ game analyzed using the Eisert–Wilkens–Lewenstein (EWL) quantization scheme. Strategies are parameterized either by a restricted two-parameter set or the full three-parameter SU(2) group.
key_observables: Payoff gaps ($P(s^*, s^*) - P(s, s^*)$), strictness of Nash equilibrium, and satisfaction of the second ESS condition.
important_parameters: The entanglement parameter $\gamma$, which controls the degree of quantum correlation in the game dynamics.
main_assumptions: The analysis is confined to a specific $2 	imes 2$ game structure and relies on comparing stability across restricted vs. full strategic domains.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the normalized Nash payoff gap confirming strictness in the restricted space for $\gamma > 0$. Figure 3 summarizes the loss of ESS status when moving from the restricted EWL domain to the full pure SU(2) space.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes that the classical game ($\gamma=0$) fails the ESS condition. It then proves stabilization in the restricted EWL space for $\gamma > 0$. Finally, it demonstrates the failure of this stability when extending the strategy set to the full SU(2) family.
why_interesting: This work explores how the mathematical structure imposed by quantum constraints (like entanglement) can stabilize dynamical equilibria that are unstable classically, highlighting the critical role of the underlying parameter space in determining emergent stability properties.
